desc:
The string words holds distinct lowercase words separated by single commas.

Word a is a predecessor of word b if you can obtain b by inserting exactly one letter anywhere into a without reordering its other letters (for example "bda" is a predecessor of "bdca"). A chain is a sequence of words from the list in which every word is a predecessor of the next one; a single word is a chain of length 1.

Return the length of the longest chain that can be built from the given words.

words = "a,b,ba,bca,bda,bdca"          -> 4   (a, ba, bda, bdca)
words = "xbc,pcxbcf,xb,cxbc,pcxbc"     -> 5   (xb, xbc, cxbc, pcxbc, pcxbcf)
words = "abcd,dbqca"                  -> 1
constraints: All words are distinct and consist of lowercase English letters
hints: A predecessor is exactly one letter shorter, so a chain strictly increases the length by one at every step. Process words from short to long.
Let best[w] be the longest chain that ends with word w. To compute it you need the best chain ending at some word that is w with one letter removed.

For each word, try deleting each of its letters in turn (at most 16 candidates); if the result is in the dictionary, take best[w] = max(best[w], best[candidate] + 1). Words sorted by length guarantee the candidates are already computed.
editorial: Sort the words by length. Keep a dictionary best mapping each processed word to the length of the longest chain ending in it. For a word w, the previous word in an optimal chain must be w with one letter deleted, so there are only len(w) candidates, each looked up in the dictionary in O(len) time. Set best[w] = 1 + max(best[c]) over the candidates that exist (or 1 if none). The answer is the largest value in best.

This avoids comparing every pair of words with a two-pointer subsequence test, which would cost O(n² · L). The deletion trick gives O(n · L²) total, about 250,000 character operations here. Because a predecessor is always strictly shorter, there are no cycles and a single pass in length order is enough.
